src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following represents the gap between two neurons?
Who were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics?
o: Robert E. Hall, Michael Woodford and Navi Pillay
Francis Halzen, Henry B. Kagan and Kenzo Soai
Anne Carson, László Krasznahorkai and Rabindranath Tagore
Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel
x: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel received the prize for work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. The tempting alternative of Francis Halzen, Henry B. Kagan and Kenzo Soai combines laureates associated with Physics and Chemistry.

s: Channelrhodopsin-2, the molecular light switch used in optogenetics, comes from which green alga?
x: Channelrhodopsin-2 comes from the green alga Chlamydomonas and opens in about 0.2 milliseconds, letting selected neurons be switched on or off with light.

s: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Francis Halzen recognised which achievement?
o: Nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis
Discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin through the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
x: Francis Halzen received the Physics prize for the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin through the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. The other options refer to Chemistry, Literature and Economic Sciences respectively.

s: Henry B. Kagan and Kenzo Soai were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in which field?
x: Kagan and Soai received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

s: Who received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for strengthening international judicial institutions and accountability for war crimes and genocide?
x: Navanethem “Navi” Pillay of South Africa received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for strengthening international judicial institutions and accountability for war crimes and genocide. Jørgen Watne Frydnes announced the prize, while Henry Dunant and Frédéric Passy were the first Peace Prize recipients.

s: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for which contribution?
o: Monetary policy, inflation and central banks
Discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin
x: Hall and Woodford were recognised for the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation. Employment, unemployment and consumption describe Hall’s subject, while monetary policy, inflation and central banks describe Woodford’s subject.

s: Who received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature?
x: Anne Carson of Canada won the 2026 Literature prize for creative writing exploring new forms; László Krasznahorkai was the 2025 winner.

s: Who proposed using light to control neurons in the 1970s, an idea behind optogenetics?
x: Francis Crick proposed light-based control of neurons in the 1970s.

s: Which Nobel Prize category–awarding body pair is correctly matched?
o: Physics – Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet
Peace – Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
Physiology or Medicine – Norwegian Nobel Committee
x: Literature is awarded by the Swedish Academy; Physics by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, Medicine by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet and Peace by the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

s: About the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Prize amount – 12 million SEK (about US$1.2 million)
Norwegian Nobel Committee – Five members appointed by the Storting
x: The Peace Prize ceremony is held in Oslo on 10 December 2026, not Stockholm; the other pairs are correct.

s: In which year were the Nobel Prizes first awarded?
x: The Nobel Prizes were first awarded in 1901; the Economics prize was created in 1968 by Sweden's central bank.

s: Who was the first woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature?
x: Selma Lagerlöf was the first woman Literature laureate; Sully Prudhomme was the first recipient and Tagore (1913) the first Asian.

s: In which year did Rabindranath Tagore become the first Indian Nobel laureate?
x: Tagore won the Literature prize in 1913; Mother Teresa became the first Indian woman laureate in 1979.

s: The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, created by Sveriges Riksbank in 1968, was first awarded in which year?
x: The Economics prize was created in 1968 and first given in 1969 to Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen; it is not one of the five prizes of Nobel's 1895 will.

s: What was the prize money of each Nobel Prize in 2026?
x: Each 2026 Nobel Prize carried 12 million Swedish kronor (about US$1.2 million).

s: Who appoints the five-member Norwegian Nobel Committee, which awards the Peace Prize?
x: The Norwegian Nobel Committee is appointed by the Storting, Norway's Parliament; the Peace Prize is presented in Oslo.

s: At most how many laureates can share a single Nobel Prize?
x: A Nobel Prize can be shared by at most three laureates.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Nobel Prizes:
1. The first Literature prize went to Sully Prudhomme in 1901.
2. Har Gobind Khorana was the first Indian-origin laureate in Medicine.
3. Nineteen women have won the Literature prize.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Sully Prudhomme (1901) was the first Literature laureate, Khorana (1968) the first Indian-origin Medicine laureate, and 19 women have won Literature.

s: Who were the first recipients of the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1969?
x: The Riksbank prize, created in 1968, was first given in 1969 to Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen.

s: In which field did V. Ramakrishnan win the Nobel Prize in 2009?
x: V. Ramakrishnan won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on the structure of the ribosome.

s: Who was the first Indian woman to win a Nobel Prize?
x: Mother Teresa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979, the first Indian woman laureate.

s: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature 2025?
x: László Krasznahorkai (Hungary) won in 2025; Anne Carson (Canada) won in 2026.

s: Who was the first recipient of the Nobel Prize in Literature (1901)?
x: Sully Prudhomme of France got the first Literature prize in 1901; Selma Lagerlöf was the first woman (1909).

s: Who won the Nobel Peace Prize 2025?
x: María Corina Machado of Venezuela won in 2025 for the democracy movement; Navi Pillay won in 2026.

s: Who was the first Indian-origin laureate of the Nobel Prize in Medicine (1968)?
x: Har Gobind Khorana (1968) was the first Indian-origin Medicine laureate.

s: Dr Karim Maredia, an Indian-origin scientist at Michigan State University, received which award?
x: Dr Karim Maredia received the Borlaug CAST Award, to be presented on December 10 at the Library of Congress in Washington.

s: Who was selected for the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award 2026?
x: Sarah Peluse, Associate Professor at Stanford University, USA, was selected for the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award 2026. Mahesh Kakde was the recipient of the 2026 Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries?
o: The prize has an age limit of 32 years or below
Mahesh Kakde became the fifth Indian winner
It was instituted in 2005 with ICTP, IMU and DST
Its age limit is below 45 years
x: The Ramanujan Prize age limit is below 45 years; the limit of 32 years or below belongs to the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award.

s: With reference to the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award 2026, which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The age limit for the award is 35 years or below.
The award is to be presented on 22 December 2026 at the SASTRA campus, Kumbakonam.
Sarah Peluse was selected on 25 September 2026.
x: The incorrect statement gives the age limit as 35 years or below; the actual limit is 32 years or below. The selection date, presentation details and year of institution stated in the other options are correct.

s: Which organisation instituted the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award?
o: International Centre for Theoretical Physics, Trieste, Italy
x: The SASTRA–Ramanujan Award was instituted by SASTRA Deemed University, Thanjavur. Stanford University is associated with Sarah Peluse, while IISc and ICTP are associated with the Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians.

s: Along with a citation, what prize does the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award carry?
x: The SASTRA–Ramanujan Award carries USD 10,000 and a citation.

s: Who received the 2026 Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries?
x: Mahesh Kakde, Professor at IISc Bengaluru, received the 2026 prize; Sarah Peluse was selected for the SASTRA–Ramanujan Award 2026.

s: Who received the INAE Lifetime Contribution Award in Engineering 2026?
x: V.K. Saraswat was named for the INAE Lifetime Contribution Award 2026; INAE is headquartered in Gurugram.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the American Geophysical Union (AGU)?
o: It is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
Its 2026 awards were presented in San Francisco
Roxy Mathew Koll and Neelima Satyam were among its 2026 awardees
x: AGU was established in 1919, not 1929; the other statements are correct.

s: Dr Lokeswara Rao Sajja became the first Indian cardiac surgeon to receive which distinction?
o: Fellow of the European Society of Cardiology (FESC)
x: Dr Lokeswara Rao Sajja became the first cardiac surgeon from India to receive the Fellow of the European Society of Cardiology distinction. The other options are bravery or state honours unrelated to his FESC recognition.

s: Who was selected for the 2026 Arthur M. Bueche Award by the US National Academy of Engineering?
x: Sethuraman Panchanathan was selected for the 2026 Arthur M. Bueche Award for his work in US science and technology policy. Sarah Peluse, Karim Maredia and Salman Rushdie were associated with different awards mentioned in the September 2026 current-affairs cycle.

s: Who is identified as the Father of India's Green Revolution in the context of the Borlaug CAST Award?
x: M. S. Swaminathan is identified as the Father of India's Green Revolution. Norman Borlaug is associated with the Nobel Peace Prize and the Borlaug name, but he is not the person identified by this title in the fact.

s: In which year did Norman Borlaug receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: Norman Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2006.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Academy Awards were first held in 1929.
2. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is headquartered in Beverly Hills.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are true: the Academy Awards began in 1929 and the Academy is headquartered in Beverly Hills.

s: Who was selected for the 2024 Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
x: Veteran actor Anant Nag was selected for the 2024 Dadasaheb Phalke Award.

s: Which film was selected as India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards?
x: The Marathi thriller Gondhal was chosen as India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards. Mother India and Lagaan were earlier Indian nominees, not the 2027 official entry.

s: Which film by Nagaland filmmaker Teja Rio won the Platform Award at the Toronto International Film Festival 2026?
x: Teja Rio's debut film Angh won the Platform Award at the Toronto International Film Festival 2026. Gondhal was India's Oscar entry, whereas Angh was the only Indian film among the 12 films in the Platform competition.

s: Who directed the Marathi thriller ‘Gondhal’?
x: Santosh Davakhar directed ‘Gondhal’. Ilaiyaraaja composed its music, while Ishita Deshmukh and Yogesh Sohoni were part of its cast.

s: Guruvayur Dorai was a mridangam maestro of which style?
x: Guruvayur Dorai belonged to the Pudukkottai style of mridangam, a school separate from the Thanjavur style.

s: Anant Nag, selected for the 2024 Dadasaheb Phalke Award, is the second Kannada actor to get it after whom?
x: Dr Rajkumar (1995) was the first Kannada actor to get the Phalke Award; Anant Nag (2024) is the second. Devika Rani was the first recipient (1969).

s: Which film was India's official entry for the 98th Academy Awards?
x: Homebound was India's entry for the 98th Oscars; Gondhal is the entry for the 99th.

s: On which date was the Sangeet Natak Akademi inaugurated?
x: The Akademi was created by a resolution of 31 May 1952 and inaugurated on 28 January 1953.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Marathi thriller 'Gondhal'?
o: Its music was composed by Ilaiyaraaja
It was directed by Santosh Davakhar
It is India's official entry for the 99th Academy Awards
x: Gondhal is a Marathi thriller, not a Tamil film. Its music is by Ilaiyaraaja, it was directed by Santosh Davakhar, and it is India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards.

s: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1969)?
x: The Phalke Award, India's highest film honour, was instituted in 1969 and first given to Devika Rani.

s: Identify the name of the creator of the popular fictional character Lord Voldemort:
x: Lord Voldemort is a villain created by British author J.K. Rowling in the Harry Potter series.

s: Who authored the book “Memorable Trials, Unforgettable Cases”, highlighted in September 2026?
x: Memorable Trials, Unforgettable Cases was authored by Justice H.N. Nagamohan Das.

s: How many couplets does the Tirukkural contain?
x: Tirukkural contains 1,330 couplets in 133 chapters.

s: Which former Chief Justice of India received the Kalinga Ratna Award from Sarala Sahitya Sansad, Cuttack?
x: Former CJI Dipak Misra received the Kalinga Ratna Award from Sarala Sahitya Sansad, Cuttack. Justice Ranjan Gogoi was the CJI who followed him, while Justice J.S. Khehar preceded him and Justice Surya Kant is the current CJI.

s: Which organisation, established in 1989 in New York City, runs the National Book Awards?
x: The National Book Foundation, established in 1989 in New York City, runs the National Book Awards.

s: The Russian translation of the Tirukkural gifted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Putin was translated by whom?
x: Naira Mkrtchyan translated the Russian edition of the Tirukkural gifted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Putin. Ankuran Dutta and Nani Gopal Mahanta were associated with the Bhupen Hazarika volume, not this translation.

s: In which year was the RSS founded by K.B. Hedgewar in Nagpur?
x: K.B. Hedgewar founded the RSS in Nagpur in 1925.

s: What prize money will the Booker Prize 2026 winner, due on 9 November 2026, receive?
x: The Booker Prize carries £50,000; the 2026 shortlist of six came from a longlist of 13.

s: Dr Ramachandra Behera received the Sarala Samman of Sarala Sahitya Sansad, Cuttack, for six decades of work in which literature?
x: Ramachandra Behera got the Sarala Samman for six decades of Odia literature.

s: Which author was chosen for the US National Book Foundation Lifetime Achievement Award in 2026?
x: Salman Rushdie, born in Bombay in 1947, is the 39th recipient and only the 4th born outside the US.

s: Who wrote 'A Century of Service – The RSS in 100 Acts of Seva'?
x: The book is by Dr Tamilisai Soundararajan, ex-Governor of Telangana; it was released by VP C.P. Radhakrishnan.

s: Sachin Tendulkar holds which UNICEF position?
o: UNICEF East Asia and Pacific Regional Ambassador
x: Sachin Tendulkar is the UNICEF South Asia Regional Ambassador; UNICEF India Celebrity Advocate is the role given to Smriti Mandhana.

s: With reference to Sunil Bharti Mittal's Legion of Honour recognition, which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: He was selected by Emmanuel Macron on 12 October 2026.
The insignia was presented at the French Embassy in New Delhi on 28 October 2026.
The Legion of Honour is France's highest award.
He received the rank of Officier.
x: The incorrect statement changes the rank to Officier; Sunil Bharti Mittal was selected in the rank of Chevalier. The selection authority, dates, venue and status of the Legion of Honour are correctly stated in the other options.

s: Which honour was announced by the Gujarat Chief Minister for Captain Smith Machhar's courage during the flydubai incident?
x: Captain Smith Machhar received the Vishisht Gujarat Garima Award for courage during the flydubai incident. The Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism was announced by Israel, while the special postal cover was issued by India Post.

s: On 11 October 2026, Smriti Mandhana was appointed to which UNICEF role?
x: Smriti Mandhana was appointed UNICEF India Celebrity Advocate on the Day of the Girl Child; South Asia Regional Ambassador is Sachin Tendulkar's role.

s: Which Israeli honour was announced for Captain Smith Machhar for saving more than 170 passengers and crew?
o: First Class Order of Zayed II
x: Israel announced its Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism for him; the Presidential Medal of Distinction is Israel's highest civilian honour, not his award.

s: In the ascending order of ranks of France’s Legion of Honour, which is the first rank?
x: Chevalier is the first rank in the ascending order: Chevalier, Officier, Commandeur, Grand Officier and Grand-Croix. Officier is the next rank, making it the most likely trap.

s: The India–France Strategic Partnership was established in which year?
x: The India–France Strategic Partnership dates from 1998. The years 2007, 2014 and 2023 do not represent the establishment year of this partnership.

s: Z.T. Lalrithangi, named among FAO's '100 Women Heroes' in agrifood systems in 2026, is a farmer from which State?
x: Z.T. Lalrithangi is from Sangau village in Lawngtlai district of Mizoram.

s: Which rank of France's Legion of Honour was conferred on PM Narendra Modi in 2023?
x: PM Modi received the Grand Cross (2023), the highest rank; Sunil Bharti Mittal got the lowest rank, Chevalier.

s:
Consider the following statements about France's Legion of Honour:
1. It was founded by Napoleon in 1802.
2. Its lowest rank is Grand-Croix.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct; the lowest rank is Chevalier, and Grand-Croix is the highest.

s: In which year was Lata Mangeshkar conferred France's Legion of Honour?
x: Lata Mangeshkar got it in 2007, Shah Rukh Khan in 2014 and PM Modi (Grand Cross) in 2023.

s: Who founded France's Legion of Honour in 1802?
x: The Legion of Honour, France's highest award, was founded by Napoleon on 19 May 1802.

s: Rimo Saha won the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award 2024 in which category?
x: Rimo Saha won in Water Adventure; Baljeet Kaur and Skaljang Rigzin won in Land Adventure, and Shiva Prasad Chamoli in Lifetime Achievement.

s: Which of the following is NOT a category of the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards?
x: The categories include Land, Water and Air Adventure; Mountain Adventure is not one of them.

s: Which team received the Champions Award at the FPAI Indian Football Awards 2026?
x: The Champions Award went to East Bengal FC; East Bengal women received a separate special honour for winning the IWL.

s: The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award is equivalent to which sports award?
x: The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award is equivalent to the Arjuna Award and includes a bronze statuette.

s: In which year were the National Adventure Awards renamed the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards?
x: The awards were renamed in 2003. The period 1993–94 refers to their institution, while 1995 was the year of their first presentation.

s: At the FPAI Indian Football Awards 2026, which team received a special honour for winning the IWL?
x: East Bengal women received a special honour for winning the IWL. East Bengal FC received the Champions Award for the ISL 2025–26, which is a separate recognition.

s: What cash prize does the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award carry?
x: Equal to the Arjuna Award, it carries a bronze statuette, certificate and ₹15 lakh.

s: Who was named Indian Footballer of the Year at the FPAI Indian Football Awards 2026?
x: Mizoram's Lallianzuala Chhangte won; Manisha Kalyan was Women's Player of the Year.

s: Who was named Women's Player of the Year at the FPAI Indian Football Awards 2026?
x: Manisha Kalyan (Punjab) won; Sanfida Nongrum was Women's Young Player.

s: She won the crown of Miss World in 1998 :
x: Linor Abargil was crowned Miss World in 1998. The other options are wrong: Diana Hayden won in 1997 and Aishwarya Rai in 1994.

s: Which year has been designated as the International Year of the Woman Farmer, with the FAO as the lead agency?
x: 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer, with the FAO as the lead agency. The other years are associated with different UNESCO literacy milestones, not this designation.

s: Besides a medal and a diploma, what did each laureate of the UNESCO International Literacy Prizes 2026 receive?
x: Each laureate received USD 30,000, a medal and a diploma; the prizes are linked to SDG 4.6.

s: Who won the 73rd Miss World title held in Nha Trang, Vietnam?
o: Zohery Mola of the Dominican Republic
x: Zohery Mola of the Dominican Republic won the 73rd Miss World title in Nha Trang, Vietnam. Elizabeth Rains was the first runner-up, Tanusia Shetty was the second runner-up, and Nikita Porwal of India reached the Top 40.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the inaugural Cool Leaders Awards (Global Cooling Pledge Assembly 2026, Singapore)?
o: The UAE was recognised for passive cooling and heat resilience
Singapore was recognised for passive cooling and heat resilience
Dong Mingzhu was recognised for low-carbon cooling
The UAE was recognised for district cooling and cooling in climate policy
x: Passive cooling and heat resilience were Singapore's areas; the UAE was recognised for district cooling and cooling in climate policy.

s: BibloRed of Colombia, a UNESCO International Literacy Prize 2026 laureate, is linked to which initiative?
x: BibloRed is linked to Escuelas LEO; Language Friendly School belongs to the Rutu Foundation.

s: Along with India, which country holds the most Miss World titles, with six each?
x: India and Venezuela have six Miss World titles each; the United Kingdom has five and Jamaica four.

s: Where was the Global Cooling Pledge, the first global commitment focused on cooling, launched?
x: The Global Cooling Pledge was launched at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 as the first global commitment focused on cooling.

s: Which Indian Miss World winner–year pair is correctly matched?
x: Diana Hayden won in 1997; Reita Faria won in 1966, Aishwarya Rai in 1994 and Yukta Mookhey in 1999.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Capital of the Dominican Republic – Santo Domingo
Miss World – Founded in 1961 by Eric Morley
x: Santo Domingo is the capital of the Dominican Republic; Priyanka Chopra won in 2000, Manushi Chhillar in 2017, and Miss World began in 1951.

s: Where were the UNESCO International Literacy Prizes 2026 presented?
x: The 2026 prizes were presented in Chiapas, Mexico, under the theme 'Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity'.

s: Hat Yai City Municipality won the UNESCO Confucius Prize for Literacy 2026 for which initiative?
x: Hat Yai City Municipality won for Language for Life, while the Government of Chiapas won for Chiapas Puede.

s: Who started Miss World, which India has won six times, in 1951?
x: Miss World was founded by Eric Morley in 1951; Kiki Håkansson was its first winner and Linor Abargil the 1998 winner.

s: Who was the first winner of Miss World (1951)?
x: Kiki Håkansson of Sweden won the first Miss World in 1951.

s: Who nominated NCSC Chairman Kishor Makwana for the Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Jan Seva Puraskar 2026?
x: Makwana was nominated by the Prime Point Foundation, not the NCSC, and received the award on 9 September 2026 at the 16th Sansad Ratna Awards.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rajbhasha awards and Hindi Diwas 2026?
o: The Department of Financial Services won First Prize in the Rajbhasha Kirti Awards 2025–26 (ministries under 300 staff)
The awards were given at the 6th All India Official Language Conference, Vashi, Navi Mumbai
Article 343 provides for Hindi in the Roman script
DARPG received the Rajbhasha Utkrishtata Samman 2025–26
x: Article 343 provides for Hindi in the Devanagari script, not Roman; the other statements are correct.

s: Who received the Aryadan Muhammed–2026 Best Public Servant Award?
x: A. Revanth Reddy received the award, comprising ₹1 lakh, a citation and a memento, at Nilambur, Kerala.

s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes was established under which Article?
x: The NCSC was established under Article 338, not Article 339.

s: Which department won the First Prize of the Rajbhasha Kirti Awards 2025–26 among ministries with fewer than 300 staff?
x: The Department of Financial Services won it at the 6th All India Official Language Conference, Navi Mumbai; DARPG got the Rajbhasha Utkrishtata Samman.

s: Which organisation instituted the Sansad Ratna Awards in 2010?
x: Prime Point Foundation instituted the Sansad Ratna Awards in 2010.

s: On which date did Apollo 11 take place?
x: Apollo 11 took place on 20 July 1969; its crew was Armstrong, Aldrin and Collins.

s: Jayaprakash Narayan is associated with the Congress Socialist Party of which year?
x: JP is associated with the Congress Socialist Party of 1934.

s: Justice Dipak Misra, who received the Kalinga Ratna, served as which Chief Justice of India?
x: Dipak Misra was the 45th CJI (2017–2018), after J.S. Khehar and before Ranjan Gogoi.

s: Which of the following pairs (person in news – Padma honour) is correctly matched?
x: V.K. Saraswat holds the Padma Bhushan; Ashoke Sen and Ela Bhatt got the Padma Bhushan, and Borlaug the Padma Vibhushan (2006).

s: In which year was Charles Correa awarded the Padma Shri?
x: Charles Correa received the Padma Shri in 1972 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2006.

s: In which year did Jayaprakash Narayan, leader of the Total Revolution (1974), receive the Bharat Ratna?
x: JP was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999; Bhupen Hazarika got it posthumously in 2019.

s:
Assertion (A): Margaret Hamilton led the development of the Apollo onboard flight software at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory.
Reason (R): She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016 from Obama.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Margaret Hamilton led the Apollo onboard flight software work at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory (for NASA), and she received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016 from Barack Obama. The medal is a recognition, not the reason she led the work, so R does not explain A.

s: Who was the Chief Justice of India in October 2026?
x: Justice Surya Kant is the CJI; Dipak Misra was the 45th CJI (2017–2018).

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
s:
Eduard Buchner, who was a German chemist, is best known for which of the following?

(I) Winning the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1907

(II) Developing the kinetic theory of enzyme action

(III) Discovering cell-free fermentation
In which year did UNICEF receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: UNICEF, established in New York on 11 December 1946, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bhupen Hazarika?
o: He was born on 8 September 1926 at Sadiya
He received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2019
He received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019
He was known as the “Bard of the Brahmaputra”
x: Bhupen Hazarika received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1992 (and the Padma Vibhushan in 2012); 2019 is the year of his posthumous Bharat Ratna.

s: Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad, which received a GI tag on 8 October 2026, belongs to which State?
x: Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad is the gram-flour sweet offered to Goddess Ambaji at the Ambaji Temple in Banaskantha district, Gujarat.

s: The Ambaji Temple, a Shakti Peetha linked to the GI-tagged Mohanthal Prasad, is in which district of Gujarat?
x: The Ambaji Temple is in Banaskantha district of Gujarat.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Geographical Indications in India?
o: The GI Act, 1999 came into force on 15 September 2003
Darjeeling Tea was the first GI product of India
The GI Registry works under DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad is a sweet made of rice flour
x: Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad is made of gram flour, not rice flour; the other statements are correct.

s: Mahesh Kakde, winner of the 2026 Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries, is a professor at which institution?
x: Mahesh Kakde is a professor at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, established in 1909.

s: In October 2026, Telangana Samagra Shiksha received which ISO certification for quality management in school education?
x: Telangana Samagra Shiksha got the ISO 9001:2015 certification, a quality management standard.

s: In which year was Samagra Shiksha, under the Ministry of Education, launched?
x: Samagra Shiksha was launched in 2018; NIPUN Bharat came in 2021.

s: In October 2026, SBI was named the World's Best Consumer Bank 2026 for the second consecutive year by which magazine?
x: Global Finance magazine (est. 1987, HQ Manhattan, New York) named SBI the World's Best Consumer Bank 2026.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Bank of India (SBI)?
o: It was formed by nationalising the Imperial Bank of India
It received the World's Best Consumer Bank 2026 award in Singapore
x: SBI received the award at the World's Best Bank Awards in Bangkok, during the IMF Annual Meetings, not in Singapore.

s: Reema Nanavaty, who received the Hillary Rodham Clinton Award-2026, is Director of which organisation?
